title: Saladin Sends Horses to Richard at Jaffa
text:
In the summer of 1192, during the Third Crusade, Saladin made a surprise attack on the port of Jaffa, recently taken by the crusaders. Richard I of England sailed down the coast, waded ashore with a small force and drove the attackers out of the town. A few days later, on August 5, Saladin's army attacked his little camp outside the walls.

Richard had only a handful of horses. According to the crusader chronicle known as the Itinerarium, during the fighting Saladin's brother al-Adil sent him two fine horses as a gift, so that a king would not fight on foot. Richard used them in the battle, and his outnumbered spearmen and crossbowmen held their ground until the attack broke off.

The two sides had long mixed war with courtesy. Envoys passed back and forth, al-Adil and Richard had met and exchanged gifts, and negotiations never fully stopped. A month later, exhausted and with Richard ill, they agreed the Treaty of Jaffa: a three year truce that left the coast to the crusaders and allowed Christian pilgrims to visit Jerusalem.
lesson: Respect toward an opponent does not weaken you in a hard contest. It keeps your honor intact and leaves the door open for the agreement that usually has to come.
people: Saladin, al-Adil, Richard I of England
source: Itinerarium Peregrinorum et Gesta Regis Ricardi, Book 6; Baha ad-Din ibn Shaddad, The Rare and Excellent History of Saladin
caveat: The gift of horses is reported by the crusader chronicle; Muslim sources describe the battle and the courtesies between the leaders but not all its details.
